subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or documented current-scope limits with plugin workarounds?
rationale: Choosing default exclusions and protected backup contents affects restore completeness and sensitive state, and the active linked PR changes user-facing backup policy rather than only fixing a mechanical failure.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

options.title: Ship reliability first
options.body: Prioritize completing or failing clearly with progress and size guidance while deferring smart/custom exclusions to the broader backup-scope tracker.

options.title: Defer scope expansion
options.body: Document current native backup limits and point optional backup strategies to ClawHub only if maintainers intentionally keep native exclusions outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the extraction into the current backup infra implementation and are best positioned to decide the core CLI backup contract shape.
